goal.en: Control where the emphasis falls, so the reader notices what you want them to notice.
goal.ar: أن تتحكم في موضع التركيز، فيلتفت القارئ إلى ما تريده أن يلتفت إليه.

text.en: Split one sentence into two parts to spotlight an element: “Ali broke the window” → “It was Ali who broke the window.”
text.ar: نشطر الجملة إلى جزأين لتسليط الضوء على عنصر بعينه: Ali broke the window تصير It was Ali who broke the window.

head: Emphasis on
Cleft
rows: It was the cost that worried us.
It was in March that we agreed.
What we need is more time.

text.en: “What … is/was …” clefts are common in speech: “What surprised me was the price.”
text.ar: الصيغة What… is/was شائعة في الحديث: What surprised me was the price.

text.en: Do not overuse clefts. One in a paragraph lands; three in a row sound theatrical.
text.ar: لا تُكثر منها. واحدة في الفقرة تؤدي غرضها، وثلاث متتالية تبدو متكلَّفة.

text.en: English puts what the reader already knows first and the new point at the end, where the stress falls.
text.ar: تضع الإنجليزية المعلوم أولاً والجديد في النهاية، حيث يقع التركيز الطبيعي.

items.en: A supplier problem caused the delay. (the delay is the news)
items.ar: مشكلة عند المورّد سبّبت التأخير — الجديد هنا هو التأخير.

items.en: The delay was caused by a supplier problem. (the supplier is the news)
items.ar: التأخير سببه مشكلة عند المورّد — الجديد هنا هو المورّد.

text.en: This is the real reason the passive exists: it lets you reorder a sentence so the new information lands last.
text.ar: وهذا هو السبب الحقيقي لوجود المبني للمجهول: فهو يتيح إعادة ترتيب الجملة ليقع الجديد في آخرها.

text.en: When a sentence opens with a negative or restrictive adverbial, the subject and auxiliary swap: “Never have I seen …”, “Not only did they refuse …”, “Rarely does he complain.”
text.ar: إذا بدأت الجملة بظرف منفي أو حاصر، تبادل الفاعل والفعل المساعد موضعيهما: Never have I seen وNot only did they refuse وRarely does he complain.

head: Normal
Inverted (emphatic)
rows: I have never seen such a mess.
Never have I seen such a mess.
They not only refused, they complained.
Not only did they refuse, they complained.
Rarely does he complain about anything.
We realised the risk only later.
Only later did we realise the risk.

text.en: This is formal and emphatic. It belongs in writing and speeches, not in every sentence — and it is far more useful to recognise than to produce.
text.ar: هذا أسلوب رسمي توكيدي، محلّه الكتابة والخطابة لا كل جملة. والتعرّف عليه أنفع من إنتاجه.

prompt.en: Emphasise the person: “Sara found the mistake.”
prompt.ar: ركّز على الشخص: Sara found the mistake.

options: It was Sara who found the mistake.
It was Sara found the mistake there.
There was Sara who found the mistake.
Sara it was that found the mistake.

explanation.en: It + be + the element + who/that + the rest.
explanation.ar: التركيب: It مع فعل الكون ثم العنصر المُبرَز ثم who/that ثم بقية الجملة.

questions.sentence: ___ worried the board was the cost, not the timing.
options: What
That
Which
It that

explanation.en: A “what” cleft: What worried the board was the cost.
explanation.ar: صيغة الشطر بـ what: What worried the board was the cost.

prompt.en: “It was on Tuesday that the system failed.” What is being emphasised?
prompt.ar: ما العنصر المُبرَز في هذه الجملة؟

options: The day it happened.
The system that failed.
The person who reported it.
The reason for the failure.

explanation.en: Whatever sits between “It was” and “that” is the spotlight.
explanation.ar: ما يقع بين It was وthat هو محل التركيز.

prompt.en: Emphasise the cost: “The cost stopped the project.” Begin “It was ___”
prompt.ar: ركّز على التكلفة، وابدأ بـ It was

questions.answer: the cost that stopped the project
accept: the cost which stopped the project

explanation.en: The element you move into the cleft is the one the reader will notice.
explanation.ar: العنصر الذي تنقله إلى موضع الشطر هو الذي سيلتفت إليه القارئ.

prompt.en: The paragraph has been discussing the delay. Which sentence continues it best?
prompt.ar: الفقرة تتحدث عن التأخير. أي جملة أنسب لمتابعتها؟

options: The delay was caused by a fault in the supplier's system.
A fault in the supplier's system caused the delay in question.
There was a fault which caused the delay in their system.
In the supplier's system a fault caused the delay then.

explanation.en: The known topic (the delay) opens the sentence and the new information lands at the end.
explanation.ar: الموضوع المعلوم (التأخير) يفتتح الجملة، وتقع المعلومة الجديدة في نهايتها.

prompt.en: Which sentence makes the supplier the news, rather than the delay?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تجعل المورّد هو الخبر الجديد بدل التأخير؟

options: The delay was caused by a new supplier.
A new supplier caused the delay.
The new supplier is causing a delay.
There is a delay from a new supplier.

explanation.en: Putting the supplier last gives it the stress; the active version foregrounds it instead.
explanation.ar: وضع المورّد في النهاية يمنحه التركيز، أما الصيغة المعلومة فتقدّمه في البداية.

questions.answer: The decision was taken by the whole committee

explanation.en: Known topic first, the agent last where the emphasis falls.
explanation.ar: الموضوع المعلوم أولاً، والفاعل في النهاية حيث يقع التركيز.

questions.sentence: Never ___ such a badly written report.
options: have I seen
I have seen
did I saw
I did see

explanation.en: After a negative adverbial, the auxiliary comes before the subject.
explanation.ar: بعد الظرف المنفي يتقدّم الفعل المساعد على الفاعل.

questions.sentence: Not only ___ the deadline, they also went over budget.
options: did they miss
they missed
they did miss
missed they

explanation.en: “Not only” at the start forces inversion: did + subject + base verb.
explanation.ar: وقوع Not only في البداية يوجب القلب: did ثم الفاعل ثم الفعل المجرد.

options: Rarely he complains about the workload.
Rarely does he complain about the workload.
He rarely complains about the heavy workload.
Only later did we realise the real risk.

explanation.en: Once “rarely” is fronted, inversion is required: Rarely does he complain.
explanation.ar: إذا تقدّمت rarely وجب القلب: Rarely does he complain.

prompt.en: Where would “Never have I seen such support” fit naturally?
prompt.ar: أين تناسب جملة Never have I seen such support؟

options: In a speech or a written tribute.
In a quick message to a friend.
In a technical instruction manual.
In a form asking for your address.

explanation.en: Inversion is emphatic and formal — right for rhetoric, wrong for a text message.
explanation.ar: القلب أسلوب توكيدي رسمي، يصلح للخطابة ولا يصلح لرسالة سريعة.

prompt.en: Make it emphatic: “I have never heard such nonsense.” Begin “Never ___”

explanation.en: Front the adverbial, then swap the subject and the auxiliary.
explanation.ar: قدّم الظرف ثم بادل بين الفاعل والفعل المساعد.

prompt.en: Match the structure with what it emphasises.

pairs: It was the cost that stopped us.
It was in May that we met.

explanation.en: Each structure moves one element into the spotlight and leaves the rest in shadow.
explanation.ar: كل تركيب ينقل عنصراً واحداً إلى بؤرة الضوء ويترك البقية في الظل.

prompt.en: Which opening sentence works best for a paragraph about your team?
prompt.ar: أي جملة افتتاحية أنسب لفقرة عن فريقك؟

options: Our team has changed considerably over the past year.
Over the past year considerable change has our team seen.
There has been changed our team over the past year.
Considerably changed over the past year has our team.

explanation.en: Normal order carries most writing; save inversion for the moment you truly want emphasis.
explanation.ar: الترتيب الطبيعي يحمل معظم الكتابة، واحفظ القلب للحظة التي تريد فيها توكيداً حقيقياً.

prompt.en: “It wasn't the price that put me off.” What does this imply?
prompt.ar: ماذا تُلمح جملة It wasn't the price that put me off؟

options: Something else put me off.
Nothing put me off at all.
The price was extremely low.
I decided to buy it anyway.

explanation.en: A negative cleft denies one cause and implies another — the reader expects it next.
explanation.ar: الشطر المنفي ينفي سبباً ويُلمح إلى سبب آخر، ويتوقع القارئ ذكره بعده.
